Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: GroundTruth: on‑prem commercial alignment & support banding

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the SOW draft. A couple of questions from our side before we loop legal:

- Platform fee: can you confirm whether the platform fee is a flat annual charge per site or if it can be amortized across a multi‑site pilot? Our CFO prefers to avoid a large upfront P&L hit for the pilot.
- Support tiers: we need 24x7 L2 escalation for the first 90 days, then drop to business‑hours for L2 after go‑live unless we keep an oncall retainer. What options do you have for a temporary elevated SRE retainer?
- Licensing: would you consider a per‑GPU operator license for our GPU‑heavy inference at edge sites vs an unlimited site license?

Can you folks propose a short table of options (pilot amortization, short‑term SRE retainer, operator vs site licensing) so we can review internally?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Lin
Head of Platform Engineering, GroundTruth Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lin <emma.lin@groundtruth.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: GroundTruth: on‑prem commercial alignment & support banding

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick answers up front, then attached a short options table in the SOW PDF and the usage workbook (estimates):

- Platform fee: we can amortize the platform fee across a defined pilot term (typically 6 months) and apply the remainder to production renewal. For pilots <=6 months we offer a 50% amortization option; for pilots 6–12 months we can stretch to 33% amortization.
- Support tiers / temporary SRE retainer: we can provide a 90‑day elevated SRE retainer (24x7 L2 + weekly oncall reviews) priced as a fixed monthly retainer that sunsets unless you opt to convert to an ongoing retainer. I put two tier options in the SOW: Retainer A (dedicated 24x7 L2, weekly ops review) and Retainer B (oncall rotation, business hours primary).
- Licensing: operator (per‑GPU) licensing vs site license: operator licenses work well where you have predictable per‑GPU consumption and want to scale incrementally; site licenses are better when you expect heavy on‑site inference and want cost predictability. I included an example TCO row in the workbook comparing the two.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Internal alignment from your procurement on whether they prefer amortization or immediate billing.
2) If amortization preferred, which pilot horizon (3/6/9 months).
3) We'll update SOW and produce a DocuSign link.

Cc'ing Ben and David to confirm pricing bands and to propose a concrete dollar table for each option by EOD tomorrow.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0198

Subject: Re: GroundTruth: on‑prem commercial alignment & support banding

Hi all —

Following Marissa's note, attaching the quick pricing bands here (see also the SOW PDF):

Option 1 — Pilot amortized (6 months)
- Platform fee: $60,000 annual list → amortized 50% for pilot = bill $30k over pilot (monthly: $5k)
- Operator licenses: $2,500/GPU/month (applies to GPUs used in pilot)
- Temporary SRE retainer (90 days): $18,000 flat (24x7 L2 coverage)

Option 2 — Immediate billing
- Platform fee: $60,000 up front
- Operator licenses: same unit pricing
- Temp SRE retainer discounted 10% if platform fee paid upfront

Option 3 — Site license (annual)
- Site license: $120,000/year per site (includes up to 10 GPUs), lowers per‑GPU economics for high utilization
- Oncall retainer optional: $6,000/month

Notes / concessions we can offer for a new strategic health customer:
- 10% pilot discount on operator licensing if they commit to a production renewal within 9 months.
- Waive DocuSign fee and include one professional services day for onboarding.

Emma — can you confirm expected GPU count for initial pilot so we can firm the operator license line (I used a placeholder of 8 GPUs in the worksheet)?

Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
ben@redwood.ai | +1 628 555 0133

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick answers:

- Pilot size: expecting 6 pilot sites, ~4 GPUs/site initially (so ~24 GPUs).
- Procurement leans toward amortization to fit Q2 pilot budget. 6 month pilot looks good.
- We'd like the 90‑day elevated SRE retainer as described; confirm handover playbook at day 75 so our ops team has a 2‑week overlap.

Can you update the SOW with the amortized platform fee, operator licensing at 24 GPUs, the 10% pilot licensing discount contingent on production renewal within 9 months, and the handover playbook milestone? If legal needs redlines we'll route Aaron.

If you can get that updated SOW and a DocuSign link by EOD Monday we can escalate for procurement sign‑off.

Emma
